title: Dose-related psychotic symptoms in chronic methamphetamine users: Evidence from a prospective longitudinal study

claims.statement: In 278 people with methamphetamine dependence followed for up to 3 years, psychotic symptoms were more likely in months of methamphetamine use than in months without use in the same individuals: odds ratio 5.3 (95% CI 3.4–8.3) for any use, 4.0 (2.5–6.5) for 1–15 days and 11.2 (5.9–21.1) for 16 or more days of use in the month, after adjustment for heavy cannabis and alcohol use; predicted risk rose from about 7% of months without use to about 48% of months with 16 or more days of use. Adjusting also for concurrent unemployment, unstable housing, low income, distress and disability roughly halved the odds ratios (2.25 and 3.90).
claims.magnitude: Any use OR 5.3 (3.4–8.3); 1–15 days 4.0 (2.5–6.5); 16+ days 11.2 (5.9–21.1); predicted risk about 7% vs 48% of months; with additional adjustment for concurrent social and health factors 2.25 (1.29–3.90) and 3.90 (1.80–8.45).
